gap_severity_basis: Lack of standardized energy-efficiency measurement limits consistent assessment and reporting.
barrier_severity_basis: Measurement and disclosure limitations directly affect the ability to monitor energy performance.
environmental_impact_basis: Improved measurement can support identification and reduction of energy consumption.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Standardized KPIs, baselines and reporting procedures are generally feasible to implement.

gap_severity_basis: Different energy-efficiency indicators reduce meaningful comparison across operators.
barrier_severity_basis: Lack of comparable indicators creates a measurement and disclosure barrier.
environmental_impact_basis: Better comparability can support identification of energy-saving opportunities.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Standardized reporting and common indicators are reasonably feasible to establish.

gap_severity_basis: Different renewable-energy measures make adoption difficult to compare consistently.
barrier_severity_basis: Inconsistent measurement creates a reporting and implementation barrier.
environmental_impact_basis: Improved renewable-energy reporting can support monitoring of renewable adoption and environmental benefits.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Standardized renewable-energy reporting is reasonably feasible.

gap_severity_basis: Unresolved renewable-energy procurement mechanisms can directly constrain implementation.
barrier_severity_basis: Procurement and regulatory barriers can significantly restrict renewable-energy deployment.
environmental_impact_basis: Greater renewable-energy procurement can substantially reduce dependence on higher-emission energy sources.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Implementation may depend on regulatory, contractual and procurement mechanisms outside the operator's direct control.

gap_severity_basis: Insufficient operator-level GHG information limits assessment of emissions performance.
barrier_severity_basis: Measurement and disclosure limitations prevent reliable emissions monitoring.
environmental_impact_basis: Better GHG inventories and reporting support emissions reduction planning.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Establishing standardized GHG inventories and reporting procedures is generally feasible.

gap_severity_basis: Different GHG measures and baselines limit meaningful comparison.
barrier_severity_basis: Inconsistent measurement and reporting create a comparability barrier.
environmental_impact_basis: Comparable GHG data support identification and monitoring of emissions-reduction opportunities.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Standardized GHG boundaries, indicators and reporting procedures are reasonably feasible.

gap_severity_basis: Reported performance relative to the operator's own stated reduction pathway indicates a significant performance issue.
barrier_severity_basis: Improvement may require changes in network energy use, operational practices and emissions management.
environmental_impact_basis: GHG reduction has substantial potential environmental benefit.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Implementation may require investment and operational changes and therefore has moderate feasibility.

gap_severity_basis: Insufficient quantitative e-waste information limits assessment of recycling and disposal performance.
barrier_severity_basis: Measurement and disclosure limitations make e-waste management difficult to monitor.
environmental_impact_basis: Improved e-waste collection, recycling and disposal can reduce environmental impacts.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Improved tracking and reporting procedures are generally feasible.

gap_severity_basis: Different e-waste scopes and reporting levels reduce comparability.
barrier_severity_basis: Inconsistent definitions and reporting create a measurement and disclosure barrier.
environmental_impact_basis: Comparable e-waste data can support improved recycling and waste-management practices.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Standardized e-waste categories and reporting procedures are reasonably feasible.

gap_severity_basis: Insufficient quantitative infrastructure-sharing evidence limits assessment of implementation and environmental benefits.
barrier_severity_basis: Limited disclosure and infrastructure coordination can restrict assessment of sharing opportunities.
environmental_impact_basis: Effective infrastructure sharing can improve resource efficiency and potentially reduce duplicated infrastructure.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Implementation may require coordination among operators and other stakeholders.

gap_severity_basis: Insufficient operator-level evidence prevents assessment of progress toward policy fiberization targets.
barrier_severity_basis: Limited measurement and disclosure creates an evidence barrier.
environmental_impact_basis: Greater tower fiberization can support more efficient network infrastructure and operations.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Implementation may require network investment and coordination, giving moderate feasibility.

gap_severity_basis: Renewable-energy implementation can be constrained by government and regulatory support mechanisms.
barrier_severity_basis: External regulatory and procurement barriers can strongly affect implementation.
environmental_impact_basis: Effective support for renewable-energy procurement can enable substantial environmental benefits.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Feasibility depends partly on government, regulatory and procurement mechanisms.

gap_severity_basis: The issue represents a policy tension between network resilience and carbon-reduction objectives rather than a direct performance failure.
barrier_severity_basis: Balancing resilience requirements with emissions reduction creates an operational and policy barrier.
environmental_impact_basis: Reducing unnecessary diesel dependence can provide environmental benefits while maintaining resilience.
implementation_feasibility_basis: Solutions require balancing reliability, backup requirements and alternative energy options.
